title: Implement the committed-schema generator stamp: export writes it, check gains the unattributable outcome
description:
Implements the mechanism specified in docs/specs/committed-schema-generator-stamp.md (LCLI-563), which is the spec half of OPAG-354 item 3. Split out because the five deliverables -- spec, export writing the stamp, check's third outcome and its exit code, the post-change churn re-measurement, and the rollout note -- do not fit one pull request under the SDLC size ceiling. Split endorsed by opum-agent 2026-09-20. The architectural commitment is OPAG-354's and is not reopened here; the mechanism is settled in the spec and is not reopened either.

READ THE SPEC FIRST. It carries the decision table, the refutation of the set-containment refinement, and the reason a version string is not committed. The two things most likely to be got wrong without it:

1. THE DIGEST IS THE DECISION KEY AND NO VERSION IS COMMITTED. schemaDriftFindings compares committed against regenerated bytes with a plain inequality (src/core/check.ts:794-829), so a committed version field is rewritten by every release in every repository whether or not the profile changed -- 21 informationless rewrites across v0.6.1/v0.6.2/v0.7.0 on this repository's own measured history. The running binary supplies its own version for the message. Ruling by opum-agent, 2026-09-20.

2. PRUNE IS ADVISED ONLY WHEN THE BINARY CAN AFFIRM IT OWNS THE ARTIFACT. Orphan plus a matching stamp digest is a real finding; orphan plus a differing stamp, and orphan plus NO stamp, are both the third outcome and never a prune. The no-stamp case is the COMMON case on the release that introduces this -- all 71 committed schemas fleet-wide are unstamped today -- so it is the default path, not an edge case.

WHERE THE CODE IS. Emission is emitSchemaFiles (src/core/schema.ts:676-694), which is the single source lore init and lore schema export share, so a scaffolded file and a re-exported one stay byte-identical -- the stamp has to land there, and it has to land on the alias files a renamed type emits (LCLI-553) or they report as drifted. The drift decision is schemaDriftFindings (src/core/check.ts:794-829), called via schemaDriftForRoot from src/commands/check.ts:239.

THE ASYMMETRY IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT A STYLE NOTE (OPAG-354 item 5). "No longer matches what this profile generates" rewrites a file and git recovers it; "no type owns this schema -- prune it" deletes one. They must not converge on one message or one exit code as the implementation grows.

TESTING THIS NEEDS THE PAIR, NOT THE PASS. The gate must be shown to REJECT (an orphan with an unrecognised stamp does not advise a prune, and exits distinguishably) and to ACCEPT (a clean stamped bundle exits 0), as two separate measurements, with the other checks green on both. A suite that only proves the new outcome fires cannot tell a working gate from one that is always in the third state -- which is the failure mode this whole mechanism is about, one level up.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore schema export writes x-lore-generator.profileDigest into every emitted file, including the byte-identical alias files a renamed type emits (LCLI-553)
lore check keys its prune/no-prune decision on the stamp rather than on type ownership alone

An orphaned schema whose stamp the running binary does not recognise -- INCLUDING one carrying no stamp at all -- produces a third outcome distinguishable in the exit code from both clean and drifted, and NEVER suggests pruning
The rewrite case and the delete case stay distinguishable in both message and exit code, preserving the asymmetry OPAG-354 item 5 names
The exit code chosen for the third outcome is reconciled with the documented set in ADR-0005 (0/2/3/4/5/6), and the CLI-contract change is recorded rather than assumed
The gate is proven to REJECT and to ACCEPT as two separate measurements, with the other checks green on both commits
The churn cost is re-measured against this repository tags AFTER the change and stated, so the objection is closed with a number rather than a judgement
A rollout note ships with the release that introduces it, since all 71 committed schemas fleet-wide go unattributable at once -- LCLI-545 records what that felt like at 0.8.0
